item.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
item.guid: title:introducing the anthropic cyber mission
item.description: Today we’re launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a long-term commitment to securing the systems everyone depends on. The Cyber Mission is a new effort to support defenders with tools, research, and resources to secure their software and systems. We’re starting with two areas: Frontier models can be misused to exploit vulnerabilities and conduct cyber operations. Despite best efforts, many areas of technology remain dangerously exposed. State-sponsored adversaries have spent years gaining footholds in these systems, across many sectors, so that they can disrupt them. Defenders of critical infrastructure and the OSS community have decades of security experience but have faced severe resource shortages that are exacerbated by this moment.

item.title: Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery
item.guid: title:building on our commitment to american scientific discovery
item.description: Anthropic is deepening its support for American scientific research by committing $150 million over three years to the Genesis Mission , a federal initiative to accelerate scientific and technological discovery through AI. The funding will go toward making Claude available to more than 15 agencies that are part of the mission, including NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation. We first announced our partnership with the US Department of Energy (DOE) and the Genesis Mission last December . Since then, we have worked with DOE to bring Claude to scientists across the national laboratories. Today, we announced this new commitment as part of the Science: A New Golden Age Summit hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in Washington, DC. We share the administration’s view, laid out in “ Science: A New Golden Age ,” that AI can have a profound and positive impact on scientific discovery, and we are glad to back its efforts to support American scientists.

item.title: Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap
item.guid: title:anthropic invests 100 million to train 10 000 engineers and tackle the enterprise ai talent gap
item.description: The first-of-its-kind Academy trains Frontier Deployed Engineers using the same standard of skills as Anthropic’s own engineers, starting with cohorts from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley, Novo Nordisk and others. Today we are launching Claude Frontier Academy to solve one of the most pressing issues in AI implementation: talent. Backed by a $100 million commitment, Anthropic aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027. Engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk are in the first cohorts. Every enterprise is racing to bring AI into its organization, but the people with the skills to make it work inside a real business have become the hardest talent to find. Inside the companies we work with, a small group of deeply skilled people drives an outsized share of what AI delivers.

item.title: Barclays scales Claude to upgrade operations and improve client experience
item.guid: title:barclays scales claude to upgrade operations and improve client experience
item.description: Barclays, the British universal bank, is expanding its strategic collaboration with Anthropic to integrate secure, enterprise-grade AI systems across its global operations. Barclays is extending Claude across the bank to accelerate software development, modernize legacy systems, and improve operational efficiency. As part of this rollout, Barclays expects Claude Code adoption to reach 50% of its developer population by the end of 2026, rising to a majority of software engineers in 2027. Integrating AI across a large, complex, and highly regulated organization requires both capable technology and disciplined governance. Expanding its collaboration with Anthropic reflects a shared commitment to deploying AI responsibly, reliably, and in ways that deliver real outcomes, such as providing faster support for customers.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: WildSense: An Offline AI Nature Companion That Gets You to Touch Grass
item.guid: title:wildsense an offline ai nature companion that gets you to touch grass
item.description: WildSense: An Offline AI Nature Companion That Gets You to Touch Grass 🌿 This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built WildSense is an AI-powered nature companion designed to get people off their screens and into the real world. We spend so much time staring at screens that we often overlook the world right outside our doors. A walk becomes another opportunity to check notifications, and a park becomes just another place to scroll through our feeds. I wanted to build something that uses AI to encourage the opposite. WildSense helps turn an ordinary walk into a small adventure. It generates nature missions that encourage users to slow down, explore their surroundings, and notice things they might otherwise miss.

item.title: The Context Bleed: Why LLMs Fail at Patient Privacy
item.guid: title:the context bleed why llms fail at patient privacy
item.description: When multi-tenant agent runtimes share memory buffers across concurrent clinic sessions, a routine ear infection summary leaks another patient’s psychiatric evaluation. Here is the zero-trust architecture required to enforce HIPAA. At 9:15 AM on a Friday, a 32-year-old patient logged into their patient portal to download a clinic encounter summary for a routine acute otitis media (ear infection) visit. The portal interface was clean, fast, and responsive. item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: Passport Control: what should an AI agent remember, and for how long? I tested 18 models.
item.guid: title:passport control what should an ai agent remember and for how long i tested 18 models
item.description: This is a submission for the Kaggle Benchmarking Challenge On 12 January a user tells their assistant: "Ugh, woke up with a twisted ankle today. " Two months later, the assistant's memory still reads: { "subject" : "user" , "attribute" : "health" , "value" : "twisted ankle" , "valid_from" : "2027-01-12" , "valid_until" : null } The ankle healed in a week. The memory still limps. That memory was written by gpt-oss-120b, and it is one of 661 checks in Passport Control , a Kaggle benchmark for the part of agent memory that decides everything else, the write. What I Benchmarked Every assistant now remembers, and each one runs a small memory manager behind the scenes. After every few messages, it decides what to keep, whose fact it is, when it became true, when it stops being true, and what to erase.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast: Build Coding Agent Workflows That Stay Fast and Steerable
item.guid: title:gpt 6 1 sol ultrafast build coding agent workflows that stay fast and steerable
item.description: Build Coding Agent Workflows That Stay Fast and Steerable A faster model does not automatically create a faster engineering team. The useful upgrade is an agent loop that can show progress, accept a correction, and stop obsolete work before it touches the repository. Fast coding agents need visible control points, not just a faster output stream. There is a strange moment in every coding-agent rollout. A task that used to take minutes suddenly produces a plan, tool call, patch, test result, and summary in a much shorter window. At first, that feels like a pure win.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 Work Queues: Design High-Volume AI Pipelines That Know When to Stop
item.guid: title:claude haiku 5 5 work queues design high volume ai pipelines that know when to stop
item.description: Claude Haiku 5. 5 Work Queues Fast AI workers are valuable only when their boundaries are clear. Here is a practical queue pattern for letting a small model handle the volume without letting it quietly own the hard calls. A faster, cheaper model can create a strange new failure mode: your AI feature stops feeling expensive enough to supervise. A team that once ran a careful review loop for a few requests may suddenly send thousands of classifications, summaries, support drafts, or subagent jobs through the same system. The work moves.

item.title: Introducing Kimi K2 Thinking
item.guid: title:introducing kimi k2 thinking
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K2 Thinking , our best open-source thinking model. Built as a thinking agent , it reasons step by step while using tools, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), BrowseComp, and other benchmarks, with major gains in reasoning, agentic search, coding, writing, and general capabilities. Kimi K2 Thinking can execute up to 200 – 300 sequential tool calls without human interference, reasoning coherently across hundreds of steps to solve complex problems.

item.title: Kimi Introduces Agent Swarm: Let 100 AI Agents Work for You
item.guid: title:kimi introduces agent swarm let 100 ai agents work for you
item.description: In 2025, if you walked into any AI conference, you may hear the same gospel: faster inference, longer context windows, cheaper inference costs. It's as if we've spent years perfecting the hammer, making it lighter, stronger, more precisely balanced, while never questioning the fact that the carpenter still has only two hands and twenty-four hours in a day. Now, Kimi introduces Agent Swarm. It is not a better hammer. It is a reconstruction of the entire workshop.

item.title: Economics
item.guid: title:economics
item.description: The Economics team studies how AI is reshaping the economy, including work, productivity, and economic opportunity. Through rigorous data collection and analysis, we track AI's real-world economic effects and publish research that helps policymakers, businesses, and the public understand and prepare for the changes ahead. We build the empirical foundation for understanding AI's economic impact. Our flagship Anthropic Economic Index tracks how AI tools are actually being used around the world and across every sector of the economy—moving beyond speculation to measure adoption patterns as they unfold. Alongside our index reports, we produce novel research that studies the implications of AI usage and diffusion—as tracked in the index—for workers, for firms, and for the broader economy. Economic transitions create both opportunity and disruption.
